identity.title: expected-quote-identity@1
identity.description: Immutable identity of an expected quotation: original source digest, parser@major, exact selector and raw byte span. No width, whitespace or synonym folding.

anyOf.title: quote-evidence@1
anyOf.description: Verbatim quote paired with its original-byte identity; presence and item ownership are checked at the Hub boundary.

quote.title: feeding-quote@1

anyOf.title: fed-pitfall@1
anyOf.description: Circle operation record of a lesson. Identity is the canonical phenomenon, suggestion and quotation, exact capture artifact, and declared bed/device. Version binding, lease evidence and collector are outside identity. The grade is a declaration and is not evidence. Hub fills the binding and refuses a model-reported version.

anyOf.title: version-binding@1
anyOf.description: Direct bindings only. Source structure requires verbatim source evidence and a declared grammar; a declaration requires the actual actor and run. Targets/usages do not create bindings. Conflict candidates are preserved, never resolved by the Hub.

anyOf.title: usage@1
anyOf.description: An observed object use in a run; line is the runtime target only and confers no version binding.

anyOf.title: feeding-offset@1
anyOf.description: Append-only layer sequence frozen with the run root. Replays read the same object horizon; later retractions still invalidate withdrawn evidence.

anyOf.title: retraction@1
anyOf.description: Administrator-only append-only correction; exactly one target set, reason is one line. A revoked account creates a deduplicated control-console todo, not an automatic erasure.

feeding.title: knowledge-structure@1
feeding.description: Closed versioned family of feeding object projections, Circle operation records (observation, procedure, pitfall), direct binding claims, usages, frozen offsets and administrator retractions beside seedlings. Identity, authorization, quotation and closed-set membership are boundary checks; nothing enters root content hashes. Operation-record identity is only the canonical statement and quotations.
